papers.title: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues
papers.abstract: GUI grounding requires locating small controls in cluttered screenshots and identifying which control a natural-language instruction refers to. Cropping and enlargement can expose local detail, but the resulting image may still leave ambiguity about the intended target. We propose PreView, an auxiliary preprocessor that improves the inputs to an existing grounding model without further training that model. PreView prepares two complementary types of input features: task-relevant views for localization and candidate-specific cues for target understanding. A trained lightweight auxiliary model predicts and refines a center, crops the screenshot into a local view, and enlarges that view for zoomed-in grounding. It also prepares a visual cue (i.e., a red-circle marker with a location hint) and a textual cue describing the candidate's identity or function. The frozen grounding model uses the prepared inputs to predict the final click. Across five benchmarks, PreView improves the average grounding accuracy of Qwen3-VL-2B, OS-Atlas-4B, and Qwen3-VL-4B without further training these grounding models. Extensive analyses examine the contributions of views and cues, center refinement, and visual input budgets.
papers.ranking_reason: This paper shows how to help AI understand phone and computer screens better so anyone can use them easily.
papers.explanation: This paper created a tool called PreView that helps AI look at cluttered phone and computer screens. It crops and enlarges small buttons and adds visual hints so the AI can click the right spot without needing extra training.
papers.why_it_matters: It teaches you how to improve computer vision inputs using simple preprocessing instead of retraining massive AI models from scratch.

project_idea.title: Smart Screenshot Cropper

project_idea.no_code_version: Use an automated workflow tool with built-in image manipulation actions to crop and save specific regions of uploaded screenshots into a folder.

papers.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps
papers.abstract: While frontier vision-language models demonstrate strong capabilities in user interface (UI) navigation, their high inference costs prohibit everyday use. Conversely, smaller models trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or offline reinforcement learning often memorize static trajectories, leading to brittle execution and an inability to recover from errors. To address these limitations, we propose a novel online reinforcement learning framework that trains UI navigation agents directly on live iOS applications. Our framework decouples the agent into two specialized components: a Planning agent and a UI Grounding model. We rely on an LLM-as-a-Judge to provide comprehensive reward signals, combining dense, step-level feedback to evaluate intermediate progress with a terminal reward for overall task completion. To effectively leverage this dual reward structure, we optimize the agent using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with step-level advantage estimation. Furthermore, we introduce GiGPPO, a novel neighbor-conditioned value estimation method that improves critic stability by leveraging reward signals from visually similar states across concurrent trajectories. To support this online training paradigm at scale, we introduce an efficient infrastructure that orchestrates hundreds of concurrent virtual iOS devices. Evaluations on rigorous benchmarks, including UINavBench, iOSWorld, and AndroidWorld, demonstrate that our online RL trained agents substantially outperform both SFT and terminal-only RL baselines while accelerating training convergence. Notably, our 8B RL agents achieve nearly a sevenfold improvement over the SFT baseline in out-of-distribution generalization to Android environments, while outperforming Gemini-3.5-Flash and tying with Gemini-3.1-Pro on real iOS applications.
papers.ranking_reason: This study explores how AI agents can navigate phone apps smoothly to help people complete everyday tasks.
papers.explanation: This study built an AI agent that learns how to tap through live phone apps using reinforcement learning [RL, a type of machine learning where software agents learn by trial and error to achieve a goal]. It splits the task into a planning part and a screen-clicking part to make app navigation much smoother.
papers.why_it_matters: It shows how splitting complex AI tasks into smaller specialized steps makes them work better on real mobile devices.

project_idea.title: App Navigation Logger
project_idea.description: Build a simple script that records button clicks and screen states on an emulator, then gives a reward score based on whether the task was completed. You will learn the basics of training agents using trial and error.
project_idea.no_code_version: Connect a mobile testing platform to a spreadsheet to log app screen names and user journey paths automatically.

papers.title: Human--AI Interactions as First-Class Data: A Formal Interaction Model and Runtime for Explainable AI Collaboration
papers.abstract: AI assistants are increasingly embedded in computational notebooks, scientific workflows, software engineering tools, and learning systems, yet human-AI interactions are often treated as transient prompt-response exchanges rather than durable data products, hindering reproducibility, explainability, replay, behavioral analysis, and adaptive AI support. We argue that these interactions form a new data class requiring formal representation and introduce the Human-AI Interaction Description Language (HAIDL), a formal interaction model with a Backus-Naur Form-inspired concrete syntax. HAIDL encodes each interaction as a structured object capturing computational context, user request, prompt payload, AI response, feedback, problem context, provenance, and model metadata. We integrate this vision into HAIDL-X, a middleware for JupyterLab that instantiates HAIDL by capturing user-bot state, building contextualized prompts, interfacing with AI providers, collecting feedback, and storing interactions in a repository. We add a learning layer over HAIDL that maps interaction objects and notebook execution traces into reproducible measures of user behavior, including engagement, performance, help-seeking, error-oriented use, and learning personas. HAIDL-X provides a foundation for treating human-AI collaboration as structured, queryable, replayable, analyzable data.
papers.ranking_reason: This research explains how people and AI assistants can collaborate and keep track of their shared work steps.
papers.explanation: This research treats human and AI conversations as structured data items rather than temporary chat logs. They introduced a format called HAIDL to save prompts, AI responses, and user feedback so conversations can be replayed and analyzed later.
papers.why_it_matters: It helps you understand how to design logging systems that track how users interact with AI tools over time.

project_idea.title: Chat History JSON Saver
project_idea.description: Create a Python script that saves every prompt and AI reply into a structured JSON file with timestamps and user feedback tags. This makes your chat logs easy to search and analyze.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke
papers.abstract: Medical chart abstraction transforms unstructured clinical narratives into structured variables for research and quality monitoring. We evaluated a prompting-based large language model (LLM) framework for extracting eight clinical variables from 2,416 neurointerventional acute stroke intervention reports across three hospitals. Twenty-two instruction-tuned open-source LLMs were evaluated across architectures, model sizes, and biomedical adaptations using Quick Response and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting. Non-expert staff annotations served as the cross-model reference standard. Evaluation was restricted to report-variable pairs with a valid LLaMA3.3-70B CoT prediction and a corresponding reference label. Performance measures included extraction accuracy, inference latency, and agreement with expert adjudication. Twenty discordant cases per variable underwent review by two senior physicians and four medical students. LLaMA3.3-70B achieved the highest overall accuracy (94.8%). CoT improved performance on inference-dependent variables such as site of occlusion, while Quick Response was optimal for directly stated procedural fields. Expert adjudication showed that AI predictions were more closely aligned with expert interpretations than non-expert annotations for most variables, with intracranial angioplasty remaining a challenge. Locally deployed LLMs can support scalable clinical information extraction and retrospective stroke registry curation, with expert oversight for ambiguous cases.
papers.ranking_reason: This paper demonstrates how AI can read messy medical notes and turn them into organized data without manual coding.
papers.explanation: This paper tested how well large language models can read messy medical notes about stroke patients and turn them into neat data tables. They found that open-source models can accurately extract clinical details when given clear prompting instructions.
papers.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how to use LLMs [large language models, AI that understands and generates text] to clean up unstructured text and convert it into structured databases.

project_idea.title: Medical Note Extractor
project_idea.description: Write a Python script that takes a fake doctor's note and sends it to an LLM API with instructions to pull out specific details like patient age and symptoms into a clean JSON format.

papers.title: What Is the Role for Humans in Creative Writing? Creativity and Diversity in Human-AI Collaboration
papers.abstract: As AI agents increasingly participate in creative teamwork, writing emerges from hybrid human-AI teams. Although AI can improve the creativity of individual outputs, these gains may come at the cost of homogenization. What is the best role for human intervention? We introduce a transmission-chain paradigm inspired by cognitive models of writing, with four stages: Plan, Write, Review, and Revise. Each stage receives the previous output and passes its own forward. Using data from 333 participants across 427 stories, we compared creativity, diversity, and enjoyment across human, AI, and hybrid chains. Consistent with prior work, all-AI chains produced more creative but less diverse stories than all-human chains. Introducing a single human into an otherwise all-AI chain increased diversity depending on role. Human planning provided the best balance: it preserved AI-level creativity, increased diversity that persisted through downstream AI stages, and maintained enjoyment. We discuss implications for designing human-in-the-loop creative pipelines.
papers.ranking_reason: This study looks at how humans and AI can team up on creative writing tasks while keeping the output diverse.
papers.explanation: This study looked at human and AI teamwork in creative writing and found that letting humans handle the planning stage keeps stories diverse while letting the AI help with drafting. Pure AI writing tends to become repetitive, but human planning fixes that issue.
papers.why_it_matters: It teaches you how to design hybrid workflows where humans and AI play distinct, complementary roles in creative projects.

project_idea.title: AI Story Planner
project_idea.description: Build a web app where a user writes a story outline, and a script prompts an LLM to expand specific paragraphs. You will practice combining human input with AI generation steps.
project_idea.no_code_version: Build a multi-step form where humans write the outline in step one, and an AI block generates the story expansion in step two.
